intake: agnostic — seminary left me unable to believe the church's account and unwilling to say there is nothing; fifty years in kitchens since and it has not settled.

walk.note: That is how it happened to me; you get the story before you get the question.
Texts are written by men; if God is anywhere it is in the world, which is Aquinas's own move.
The data really does come down to testimony and a first cause, so doubt; but the hiding dilemma misreads Aquinas, whose God does will and choose.
A prayer study tests a vending machine, not being itself; no prayer effect leaves me where I was, in doubt, not in disbelief.
Granting no God, the mind still does not look like meat to me; but 'does not seem' is a feeling, not an argument.
I have watched dementia take a man's memory and his self with it; the brain does the work and nothing without it is the same person.
We just said everything is physical and now everything is mind; physics not saying what has the structure does not get you a dream.
Granting the dream, yes, somebody dreams it.
You treat the new dishwasher decently before you know anything about him; it is a choice and I make it too.
Caring ahead of proof does teach you where your knowing stops; the entropy paragraph and the mention of Claude are noise.
The author admits four doors are open and picks hope; I have stood at equanimity for fifty years and the Parfit pages do not move me off it.
The move says itself that being a maker does not make a maker resolved, so why is the next position a resolved maker?
One sentence, 'more of a bargain than an argument'; what bargain, between whom?
'A mind that attends to everything has no one home' is asserted, not shown, and Aquinas's knowing-in-one-act is the standing counterexample the text itself concedes is untouched.
A burn hurts the one burned whether or not anyone made the world; yes.
Wanting to be remembered does not hold the self apart from anything; the text admits it is a motive, not evidence, and then builds a position on it anyway.
Nothing is claimed here; it is a bookmark, not a move.

first_exit.why: I stopped where every agnostic stops: the lack of a prayer effect in a heart-surgery study tells me nothing about the God Aquinas was talking about, and absence of that kind of evidence leaves me in doubt, not in disbelief. The move changes what 'God' means between the premise and the conclusion.

comment: Moves 1 through 7 are an argument and I can follow them; from move 8 on you are choosing, and the text knows it, so say so at the top instead of burying the admissions inside the moves. Cut move 13 to a quarter of its length and move the Parfit material to a footnote; a reader who has to stand for a living will not wade through it. And classical theism does not deny that God chooses; fix that or the dilemma in move 3 falls over.
